# Ray Tracing and GPU

```
syscheck --only rt,gpu
```

## Ray tracing (CPU)

A fixed **path tracer** (a renderer that follows light rays and their bounces, the same idea used by modern ray traced graphics) draws a closed room:

* 5 walls plus a back wall (red and green side walls), 48 spheres on the floor (every sixth is a mirror), and one spherical light on the ceiling: 55 objects in total, all generated by code.
* Up to 5 bounces per ray, brute-force intersection tests, no shortcuts.
* The math uses only addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and square roots, which give exactly defined results, with an integer random number generator. The picture is therefore **bit-identical on every platform**. The program renders four reference passes and compares a checksum with the expected value. If it differs, the report warns that this platform calculates differently and that ray tracing numbers are less comparable.

The result is in **Mrays/s** (million ray segments per second, primary rays plus bounces), for one thread and for all threads.

## GPU

The GPU tests use portable compute shaders written in WGSL and run through the [`wgpu`](https://wgpu.rs) library on **Vulkan** (Linux, Windows, Android), **Metal** (macOS, iOS) or **DirectX 12** (Windows). One program therefore covers NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple and mobile GPUs.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| FP32 compute | Floating-point speed in GFLOPS (fused multiply-add) |
| Integer compute | Integer operations, Gops/s |
| Memory bandwidth | Copy speed inside GPU memory, GB/s |
| Matrix multiply | A 16x16 tiled matrix multiply (512x512 with `--quick`, 1024x1024 otherwise) in GFLOPS. The result is **checked against the CPU**; a wrong result means a driver problem and the matrix score is ignored |
| Host to GPU and GPU to host copy | Transfer speed over the bus (PCIe, or shared memory on integrated GPUs) |
| Submit latency | Round trip of a tiny GPU job, p50 and p99 in microseconds |
| Ray tracing on the GPU | The same path tracer as above, as a compute shader, in Mrays/s. The picture brightness must match the CPU reference within 3 %, otherwise the result is ignored |

### Safety: the GPU runs in a separate process

Graphics drivers sometimes crash or hang. The GPU tests therefore run in a child process of `syscheck` with a time limit (90 seconds with `--quick`, 240 seconds otherwise). If the driver crashes, only the GPU part fails; everything else is still reported and saved. Set the environment variable `SYSCHECK_GPU_DEBUG=1` to print the GPU errors the driver reports.

### Which GPUs are tested

* Up to **two adapters** are tested. Duplicates (the same GPU shown by several backends) are removed and the better ones are chosen.
* **Software renderers** (for example `llvmpipe`, `SwiftShader`, Microsoft Basic Render) are listed but **not scored**: they run on the CPU and say nothing about a real GPU.
* If no adapter is found (no graphics driver, or a container or virtual machine without GPU access), the report explains that.

### Hardware ray tracing units

The program detects whether the driver reports hardware ray tracing support and says so in the report. It does **not yet measure** those units. The ray tracing score uses the shader cores, so it can be compared between all GPUs but understates GPUs with dedicated ray tracing hardware.

### AI relevance

The AI score uses the GPU matrix multiply speed and memory bandwidth, and the amount of video memory when the system tells it. Large language models need enough video memory for their weights. If the memory size is unknown (for example on Windows today), the report says it is not included.

## Scores

The graphics and ray tracing scores come from the GPU results only. See [Scores and Verdicts](Scores-and-Verdicts.md).
